body.x: UNIUNI Corp. (CEO Sooyeon Han) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time).

UNIUNI is a deep-tech startup that has developed and commercialized “spatial safety AI” solutions that fundamentally eliminate concerns over privacy infringement. According to the company, it positions itself as a privacy-first AI company that simultaneously realizes technological innovation and personal data protection, guided by the philosophy of “safety that protects without seeing.”

In line with this value, UNIUNI successfully implemented non-vision AI technology that detects falls, abnormal behavior, and emergency situations in specific spaces without directly capturing video or images. This helps ensure user safety in locations where camera hardware use is restricted, such as public restrooms, hospitals, nursing facilities, and other multi-use spaces.

At CES 2026, UNIUNI showcased its flagship solution, “RestroomGuard Savvy.” Savvy is a non-vision spatial awareness AI solution that applies ToF (Time-of-Flight)–based 3D depth sensors and AI algorithms, delivering functionality that safeguards users in sanitary spaces within public restrooms and multi-use facilities.

The core hardware of Savvy, the ToF sensor, emits infrared light and measures the round-trip time of reflected signals, generating pixel-level distance (depth) maps from the data. Through this process, the system precisely captures changes in the shape of people or objects, movement trajectories, and dwell time.

In addition, low-resolution acoustic events such as screams, loud noises, and collision sounds, as well as abnormal air quality indicators such as smoke related to fire, serve as auxiliary signals. Using AI algorithms embedded in edge devices that analyze these inputs, the system comprehensively detects falls, assaults, illegal filming patterns, prolonged inactivity, vandalism, and signs of fire.

Furthermore, event data analyzed on the device is transmitted to control systems as anonymous metadata over encrypted channels, such as mTLS. This allows facility managers to receive immediate alerts through visual, audio, or vibration notifications and respond promptly to emergency or hazardous situations. Based on this technology that strengthens facility safety while strictly protecting user privacy, UNIUNI earned the honor of winning Innovation Awards in two categories.

At the same time, the company achieved the milestone of winning awards for two consecutive years, following last year’s recognition, and drew strong interest from global visitors at this year’s CES. These recent CES achievements are expected to have a positive impact by increasing brand awareness in domestic and overseas markets and expanding exports.

body.x: A UNIUNI official said, “After supplying the Savvy non-vision spatial awareness AI platform to various facilities in Korea and accumulating extensive references, we are currently conducting pilot projects through exports to Japan, Malaysia, and Switzerland, as well as collaborations with partners in countries around the world.” The official added, “By leveraging these country-specific export experiences and the insights and networks secured over the past two years at CES, we plan to pursue phased export expansion into major Southeast Asian countries such as Singapore and into Europe.”

The official continued, “In the mid to long term, we also plan to expand into the Americas, including the United States, and work to establish Savvy’s technology as a global standard for privacy-protective AI.” The official added, “We aim to achieve sustainable growth by expanding partnerships and customers across public safety and smart city sectors worldwide.”

The Incheon Metropolitan City Government and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority formed the “INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion” at LVCC North Hall during CES 2026, presenting Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as it evolves beyond a smart city into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs, including Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Awards Showcase, the pavilion supported the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES, including 10 companies exhibiting at the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion. In particular, 14 companies won 17 CES Innovation Awards, marking the largest achievement to date and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovative enterprises.
